note: The Viking Kingdom of Jorvik (York) emerged within the former Kingdom of Northumbria when the Great Heathen Army captured York (866) and established a Norse kingdom there. Northumbria's native English aristocracy was largely killed or displaced; subsequent Jorvik kings alternated between Norse (Halfdan Ragnarsson, Sigurd, Eric Bloodaxe) and Anglo-Danish rulers. The kingdom's instability — six kings in 20 years during the 940s-950s — reflected the competition between Viking factions and the Wessex reconquest campaign. Eric Bloodaxe's death (954) ended Jorvik and merged Northumbria into the English kingdom.

_quarry.structural_significance: Jorvik's 88-year existence as a Viking kingdom creates the Norse cultural layer in Yorkshire that persists in place names and dialect to the present; the kingdom's instability demonstrates how the Danelaw's political fragmentation prevented coordinated resistance to the Wessex reconquest
